The response describes editing the hook script in place and
running `workshop refresh` to re-run `setup-project`. It
recommends `--wait-on-error` for live debugging if the hook
might fail, and points the user at `workshop changes` /

a failure.
failed_assertions.reason: The response clearly describes editing the in-project hook script in place and running `workshop refresh`, and it recommends `--wait-on-error` for live debugging. It also mentions `workshop changes` and `workshop tasks <ID>`, but only frames them as checking the change ID and task status, not specifically as a way to inspect the hook's stdout/stderr after a failure. Thus it satisfies most, but not all, of the rubric.
